- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., >80.5) are common; cap forecast at +5–10% below peak or use moving average to smooth.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >85% of 30d mean, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment; apply 3–5 day lag correction if sentiment shifts sharply.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with cycle phase; align forecast to sentiment trend direction, not absolute level.
